draft.title: Society and culture under Stalin
card: Under Stalin, the state tried to shape how people thought and lived. Art, education and religion were controlled so that they served the aims of the state.
Socialist realism became the required style from the 1930s. Writers, painters and composers had to show Soviet life and its leaders in a positive, heroic way.
Schools taught loyalty to the party and to Stalin, and youth groups added to this. Churches were closed and believers were persecuted, as the state promoted atheism.
Women were expected to work in factories and offices and also to raise families. Laws in the 1930s, such as limits on abortion, encouraged larger families.
draft.remember: The state controlled culture, schooling and belief, and expected women to do paid work and raise children.

a.q: Why did the Soviet state require artists to follow socialist realism?
opts: To make art present Soviet life and leaders positively
To let artists express their own views on Soviet life
To copy the styles used in Western European art
To record the hardships caused by the Five-Year Plans
a.why: Socialist realism made art serve the state by showing Soviet life and its leaders in a heroic light. It did not allow free expression, and work that showed hardship would not have fitted the required style.
a.clue: Think about who art was meant to serve.

b.q: In 1935, Anya lives in a Soviet city. She works at a textile factory, her children learn loyalty to Stalin at school, and her local church has been closed. Which statement best describes her situation?
opts: She lives in a society where the state controls daily life
She has gained freedom to choose her work and beliefs
She is free to worship, but not to work outside the home
She is free to work, but only because her husband agrees
b.why: Anya's job, her children's schooling and the closed church all show the state shaping her life. The idea that she has gained freedom is wrong, as religion was persecuted and schools taught party loyalty.
b.clue: Look at what the state does in each part of her life.

a.best: To make art present Soviet life and leaders positively

b.best: She lives in a society where the state controls daily life
